turns.text: Adventures in user experience, or "why doing one bit of design well doesn't help if your user journey is broken". Featuring @VirginTrains. It started so well.

@VirginTrains This morning I got an email. I was actually pretty please with it: it recognised my previous choices, and asked me what I actually wanted. Gave me granular choices about what would be helpful to me specifically. Great.
@VirginTrains So sure. I'll tailor my info.
@VirginTrains I should say, I personally am not a fan of the writing style used here, but that's just my preference. The important part here is the content - being thoughtful about users.
@VirginTrains So far, so good. I fill in the form. Again, I think the style is overly friendly, but it doesn't get in the way, so whatever. The choices on the form are clear and well-communicated.
@user Can @user assist at all today? ^MW
@VirginTrains And here's where it goes wrong. Email? What email? There wasn't an email field in the form, and besides, we _came_ from my email, so surely should know it already.
Chrome dev tools to the rescue. Turns out, there was an input - that for some reason has "display:none" - and sure enough, it has no value.
Hilariously, I enter my email address as the value, and try to submit again - and it works fine!
My point here is - it was all going great. I felt listened to as a user, and I had actually chosen to receive some information, because they'd given me a choice that I felt would be useful to me.
@VirginTrains @user Is there anything I can help with Beth? ^KM
But all of that good comms work was undone when the form was broken.
You can put tons of work into your users comms, and do a great job. But that work gets wasted if you don't sort out the wider user journey too.
